correctness.rationale: Uniform relative order suffices. Given a record at i, the earlier relative order is still uniform, and triples strictly after i are independent. The peak at i−1 is impossible. The joint event at j=i puts the maximum of the first i+1 at i. At j=i+1 the maximum of the first i+2 must be at i+1, and the relative order of the first i must put its maximum at i; the latter has conditional probability 1/i. These give the four conditional probabilities and the claimed entries without integration. Multiplying the two frozen bidiagonal factors reproduces every entry, including the first diagonal 1/6, so their diagonal product gives the determinant. The triangular inverse recurrences give the claimed sum. Independently, its product telescopes to (i−1)i(i+1)/[(k−1)k(k+1)]; with m=max(i,j) the sum becomes 3j(i−1)i(i+1)/2 times [1/((m−1)m)−1/((n−1)n)], strictly positive even at the boundary. Invertibility gives both stated linear detection implications.
residual_risks: The frozen finite checks were inspected, not rerun: the inversion loop checks positivity and MQ=I, not explicit agreement with (3). The recurrence and telescoping above verify (3) for all sizes. The result concerns cross-covariance, not a precision matrix or nonlinear recovery.
